title: Austria by Train: Innsbruck, Kaprun and Salzburg with a Day in Hallstatt
meta_title: Austria by Train 8 Days: Innsbruck, Kaprun, Salzburg
meta_description: Relaxed 8-day Austria rail holiday: Innsbruck's Old Town, the Kaprun gorge walk, glacier and spa, Salzburg's Sound of Music tour and a day trip to Hallstatt.
hero_alt: Hallstatt village on its lake in Austria
tagline: Alpine towns, a glacier and a lake village, at an unhurried pace by train
facts: Train, with short bus and taxi links
intro: A gentle Austria holiday for travellers who like walking, scenery and good trains more than a packed schedule. Two nights in Innsbruck under the Nordkette mountains, two in the mountain village of Kaprun with a gorge walk, a glacier and a spa afternoon, then three in Salzburg for Mozart's old town, the Sound of Music tour and a day trip to Hallstatt. This combines our two suggested plans: it keeps the mountain stay at Kaprun and adds the Hallstatt day. Hallstatt is about 1 hour 15 minutes from Salzburg by car and 2 hours 30 minutes by train and bus, so we suggest a private driver for that day.
highlights: Innsbruck's Old Town, the Golden Roof and the Nordkette cable car to 2,256 m
The scenic Railjet train ride through the Tyrolean Alps

An afternoon at the Tauern Spa

days.title: The Sigmund Thun Gorge, the glacier and the spa
days.summary: A boardwalk gorge walk, a glacier view and an afternoon of thermal pools.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Sigmund Thun Gorge
rows.text: Wooden walkways and bridges above a roaring stream, 320 m long. Gentle, with a few steps.
notes: Open from about May to October; check opening on rainy days.

notes: At over 3,000 m you may feel breathless. Walk slowly and skip it if you have heart or breathing problems.
Winter jacket, gloves and sunglasses, even in June.

best_time: Late May to September. The Kaprun gorge and the glacier reservoirs open from about May, and Hallstatt is quietest in June and September.
seasons: Green valleys, waterfalls in full flow and fewer crowds; some high passes and lifts open only from late May or June.
Warmest weather and every lift open; busiest and most expensive.
Clear autumn days and quieter trains; some lifts close for maintenance from late October.
Snow and Christmas markets; skiing in the mountains, short days in the cities.
best_pick: Late May, June and September: green, mild and quieter.

faqs.q: Is this suitable for a senior couple?
faqs.a: Yes. Train journeys are short, hotels are close to stations, and every walk can be shortened. Skip the glacier if altitude is a concern.

faqs.q: Can we do it with only two hotels?
faqs.a: Yes: 3 nights in Innsbruck and 4 in Salzburg, with Hallstatt as a day trip. You lose the Kaprun mountain stay, the gorge and the spa.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

faqs.q: Do you look after vegetarian and Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and guide before you travel, and suggest pure-vegetarian restaurants along the route. Jain meals without onion, garlic and root vegetables can be arranged in most places with notice.

faqs.q: Is there support while we travel?
faqs.a: Yes. You have our 24/7 travel desk on +91 97148 59797 and +91 98242 21400 and a WhatsApp group with your consultant for the whole trip.

good_to_know.title: Hotel deposit
good_to_know.text: Use a credit card for the deposit or pre-authorisation at check-in, never a forex or debit card. Forex cards cannot hold funds, many hotels refuse them, and a credit-card hold is released faster.

good_to_know.title: Cards and cash
good_to_know.text: On card machines, always choose to pay in euros, never in INR. Cards work almost everywhere. Carry about EUR 50 in cash for small cafés, toilets and markets.

good_to_know.title: Pickpockets
good_to_know.text: Busy stations, trams and squares are pickpocket hotspots. Keep passports in the hotel safe, carry a copy, and wear your bag in front in crowds.

good_to_know.title: Plugs, water and meal times
good_to_know.text: Plugs are the two round-pin type C and F at 230 volts (Switzerland uses type J; a type C plug fits). Tap water is safe to drink. Lunch is about 12:00 to 14:00 and dinner from about 18:30.

good_to_know.title: Austrian trains
good_to_know.text: ÖBB Railjet trains are comfortable and punctual. Seat reservations cost a few euros and are worth it on Fridays and Sundays. Luggage racks are at the end of each carriage.

emergency: Embassy of India, Kärntner Ring 2, 1010 Vienna
dining_intro: Vegetarian food is easy to find in every city on this route; Jain meals take planning. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and tour, and list Indian and vegetarian restaurants near each hotel in your travel pack.
dining_avoid: Soups, sauces, risottos and even some vegetable dishes are often made with meat or fish stock, and many cheeses use animal rennet. Show the food card and ask before ordering.

We are strict vegetarians (Jain). No meat, fish, seafood or eggs. No onion, garlic, potato, carrot or any root vegetables. No meat or fish stock. Thank you.
